samples.summary:
The "stylesheet wait is load-bearing" invariant this delta documents and fixes for Slides is not applied to the Docs apply path, which the subset change newly makes race-prone.

This delta changes `applySlideFontFamily` to await `ensureFontLink`'s promise before `document.fonts.load()`, and the design docs now state the rule generally ("AWAIT IT BEFORE `document.fonts.load()`/`check()`", font-catalog.ts:156; slides-fonts.md). Docs' equivalent apply path still ignores it: `ensureFont` calls `ensureFontLink(family)` synchronously and immediately calls `store.fonts.ensureFont(family)` → `FontRegistry.ensureFont` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:293-314), which does `document.fonts.check()`/`load()` right away and then caches the family as `'loaded'` forever, with the re-layout listeners fired only on that one resolution.

Before this PR the picker's visibility observer injected the *full* family link, so by pick time the stylesheet had usually parsed and the registry's `load()` saw real faces. Now that previews are subsets which are additionally released before `onChange` (font-family-picker.tsx:198), the full link is freshly injected at pick time, so the registry's `load()` typically resolves against zero connected faces, records `'loaded'`, and never notifies the canvas again — the applied family paints in a fallback. That contradicts the issue's outcome "every previewed row and every applied font looks exactly as it does today".
searchedFor: checked all three FontFamilyPicker call sites in the Docs toolbar

samples.summary: The release-on-unmount effect (and its ~7-line rationale comment) is copy-pasted verbatim into both preview surfaces (`font-family-picker.tsx:175-178` and `more-fonts-dialog.tsx:174-177`). Since `font-catalog.ts` already owns the subset lifecycle (`ensurePreviewFontLink`, `removePreviewFontLink`, `releasePreviewFontLinks`), a single exported hook (e.g. `usePreviewFontLinks(listEl)`) alongside them would keep the borrow/release contract in one place and make a third preview surface impossible to get wrong. Taste-level; the current form is correct.

`releasePreviewFontLinks()` is a document-global blanket removal with no ownership token, justified in its docstring by "only these lists ever inject a subset, they are modal". That assumption is enforced only by comment: the Docs toolbar renders three `FontFamilyPicker` instances and the Slides theme-builder renders two adjacent ones, so any future non-modal preview surface (an "in-use fonts" strip, a theme thumbnail preview) would have its faces yanked by an unrelated menu closing. Passing the family set (or the list element) that is being released would scope it without refcounts. Preference, not a defect today.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism is unreachable in this repo. `ensureFont` in docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-355 calls `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)` through an optional chain, but no DocStore implementation has a `fonts` member (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11-51; store/memory.ts:32; packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts has zero `fonts` hits), and `FontRegistry` is never instantiated in production code anywhere (repo-wide grep: only the export at packages/docs/src/index.ts:188, the class at view/fonts.ts:278, docs, and one unit test at packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63). So the Docs apply path performs no `document.fonts.load()`/`check()` at all (grep of `document.fonts.(load|check|ready)` under packages/frontend/src matches only slides apply-font-family.ts:40 and slides/pdf-actions.ts:54) and never records a sticky `'loaded'` status — the "registry's load() resolves against zero faces, caches 'loaded' forever, never notifies the canvas" chain cannot execute. Additionally, Docs re-layout on late font arrival is driven by the non-caching `document.fonts` `loadingdone` / `fonts.ready` hook in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2663-2692, which clears the measure cache and re-renders whenever any face finishes loading, so there is no one-shot notification to miss. Ground: not-present (with an independent guard at editor.ts:2671-2676).
